narration.text: Welcome to this chapter on configuring Application Insights, a crucial service for any developer working with modern applications. In today's complex cloud environments, simply knowing if your server is up isn't enough. You need to understand how your application is performing, what users are experiencing, and where bottlenecks might occur within your code or its dependencies. Application Insights provides this deep, code-level visibility, transforming raw data into actionable insights. Throughout this lesson, we'll explore how to integrate this powerful tool into your applications, leverage its rich features for diagnostics, and even customize it to track specific business metrics. By the end, you'll be equipped to proactively monitor, troubleshoot, and optimize your applications, ensuring a robust and responsive user experience. Let's begin our journey into mastering application performance monitoring with Azure Application Insights.

screens.title: What is Application Insights?
screens.subtitle: Your Comprehensive APM Solution for Modern Applications

narration.text: Application Insights is Azure's premier Application Performance Management, or APM, service. Think of it as a specialized diagnostic tool that goes far beyond basic server monitoring. While Azure Monitor and Log Analytics provide excellent insights into your infrastructure and platform, Application Insights dives deep into the actual performance and behavior of your application code. It's designed to give you a comprehensive view of your web applications, APIs, and microservices, regardless of where they're hosted—be it Azure, on-premises, or even other cloud providers. The key differentiator is its ability to instrument your code directly, collecting rich telemetry about everything from incoming requests and external dependencies to unhandled exceptions and user interactions. This deep visibility allows you to understand not just if your application is running, but how well it's performing and what your users are truly experiencing. It's an indispensable tool for proactive troubleshooting, performance optimization, and making data-driven decisions about your application's health. What is Application Insights? means application insights is azure's apm service, providing deep, code-level monitoring for web applications, apis, and microservices, offering unparalleled visibility into performance, dependencies, and user behavior across any hosting environment.. In practical terms, your comprehensive apm solution for modern applications. A concrete example makes the pattern visible, and a brief contrast helps prevent a common misconception. Module 6›Chapter 3›What is Application Insights?
Core Concept

What is Application Insights?

Your Comprehensive APM Solution for Modern Applications

Application Performance Management (APM)

Application Insights is Azure's dedicated APM service, providing deep, code-level monitoring for web applications, APIs, and microservices. It helps you understand the internal workings and performance of your actual application code.

Beyond Infrastructure Monitoring

Unlike Azure Monitor or Log Analytics, which focus on infrastructure and platform, Application Insights instruments your code to collect rich telemetry about requests, dependencies, exceptions, and user behavior.

Key Takeaway

Application Insights is essential for gaining comprehensive, code-level visibility into your application's health and performance, enabling proactive issue resolution and optimization.

Rich Telemetry Collection

It automatically collects data on incoming HTTP requests, calls to external services (dependencies), unhandled exceptions, system performance counters, and availability, providing a holistic view.

Any Hosting Environment

Application Insights is flexible and can monitor applications hosted anywhere, including Azure, on-premises servers, or other cloud platforms, making it a versatile APM solution.

Common Misconception

Don't confuse Application Insights with basic server monitoring. While it collects some system metrics, its primary strength lies in understanding application code behavior, not just server uptime.

screens.title: Understanding Application Insights Telemetry
screens.subtitle: The Rich Data Collected by the SDK

narration.text: The true power of Application Insights stems from the rich variety of telemetry data its SDKs automatically collect from your application. Let's explore these core types. First, we have Requests, which provide detailed information about every incoming HTTP request to your web application, including its URL, response time, and whether it succeeded or failed. This is fundamental for understanding user experience. Next are Dependencies, which track all the calls your application makes to external services, such as databases, other APIs, or Azure services like Storage. Monitoring dependencies is crucial for identifying bottlenecks outside your direct code. Then there are Exceptions, which capture details about any unhandled errors in your application, complete with stack traces and the context of the request that caused them, making debugging much easier. Performance Counters give you system-level metrics like C P U and memory usage from the host machine. Availability telemetry comes from web tests that periodically ping your application, ensuring it's reachable from various global locations. Finally, and very powerfully, you can log Custom Events and Metrics, allowing you to track specific business logic or performance indicators unique to your application. Together, these telemetry types paint a comprehensive picture of your application's health and behavior.

keyIdea.title: Diverse Telemetry Collection
keyIdea.text: The Application Insights SDK automatically gathers diverse telemetry, including requests, dependencies, exceptions, performance counters, and availability, providing a holistic view of application health and user experience.

content.html:
Module 6›Chapter 3›Integrating AI into .NET
Implementation Guide

Integrating Application Insights into .NET

Enabling Automatic Telemetry Collection

// Program.cs for .NET 6+
using Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.Extensibility;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

// Add services to the container.
builder.Services.AddApplicationInsightsTelemetry(); // Automatically picks up instrumentation key

// Configure custom telemetry processor (optional)
builder.Services.AddApplicationInsightsTelemetryProcessor<MyCustomTelemetryProcessor>();

builder.Services.AddControllersWithViews();

var app = builder.Build();

// Configure the HTTP request pipeline.
if (!app.Environment.IsDevelopment())
{
    app.UseExceptionHandler("/Home/Error");
    app.UseHsts();
}

app.UseHttpsRedirection();
app.UseStaticFiles();

app.UseRouting();

app.UseAuthorization();

app.MapControllerRoute(
    name: "default",
    pattern: "{controller=Home}/{action=Index}/{id?}");

app.Run();
Add NuGet Package

Install Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.AspNetCore to bring the SDK into your .NET project.

Enable Telemetry

Call builder.Services.AddApplicationInsightsTelemetry() in Program.cs to enable automatic collection.

Connection String/Key

Provide an Instrumentation Key or Connection String via environment variables or configuration to link your app to the AI resource.

Key Takeaway

Proper SDK integration and configuration of the Instrumentation Key are fundamental for Application Insights to begin collecting and sending telemetry from your application.

narration.text: When you need immediate feedback on your application's health, especially during a new deployment or a high-traffic event, the Live Metrics Stream is your go-to tool. It provides a real-time, minute-by-minute view of critical metrics like incoming requests, failures, server C P U usage, and even custom events as they happen. This instant feedback loop is invaluable for quickly validating changes or detecting anomalies. In contrast, the Performance blade offers an aggregated, historical view of your application's performance. Here, you can analyze average response times for requests and dependencies, identify the slowest operations, and understand performance distributions over time. While Live Metrics gives you a snapshot of the present, the Performance blade helps you identify long-term trends and pinpoint specific operations that consistently underperform. Both tools are essential, but they serve different purposes: Live Metrics for immediate operational awareness, and Performance for deeper, historical analysis and optimization. Understanding when to use each will significantly enhance your diagnostic capabilities. Module 6›Chapter 3›Live Metrics & Performance
Real-time Diagnostics

Live Metrics Stream and Performance Blade

Instant Insights into Application Health and Speed

Live Metrics Stream

  • •Provides real-time, minute-by-minute view of application performance.
  • •Shows incoming requests, failures, server CPU, and custom events as they happen.
  • •Ideal for monitoring deployments, high-traffic events, and immediate anomaly detection.
Key Use Case

Use Live Metrics during a new feature rollout to instantly verify performance and catch any regressions in real-time.

Performance Blade

  • •Offers aggregated, historical views of request response times and dependency durations.
  • •Allows drilling down to specific operations to identify slow calls and their distribution.
  • •Best for identifying long-term performance trends and areas for optimization.
Misconception

Live Metrics is not a replacement for detailed historical analysis. It's a real-time pulse, while the Performance blade provides the full diagnostic history.

Key Takeaway

Live Metrics Stream provides instant operational awareness, while the Performance blade offers aggregated historical data for deeper analysis and identifying long-term optimization opportunities.

screens.title: Investigating Failures and Transactions
screens.subtitle: Pinpointing Errors and Tracing End-to-End Flows

narration.text: When your application encounters issues, Application Insights provides powerful tools to help you quickly diagnose and resolve them. The Failures blade is your first stop for understanding errors. It gives you a summary of all exceptions and failed requests, allowing you to see which error types are most prevalent, their count, and even sample stack traces. You can drill down into specific error groups to understand the context and frequency of each issue, which is crucial for prioritizing fixes. On the other hand, Transaction Search is invaluable for debugging specific user issues or understanding complex request flows. It allows you to search for individual requests, events, or exceptions and then visualize the full end-to-end transaction flow. This means you can see all associated dependencies, logs, and related telemetry for a single operation, providing a complete picture of what happened. While Failures helps you identify *what* is breaking, Transaction Search helps you understand *why* and *how* a specific interaction unfolded. Together, these tools form a robust diagnostic duo, enabling efficient troubleshooting and faster resolution of application problems. screens.title: Analyzing Dependencies and User Behavior
screens.subtitle: Identifying Bottlenecks and Understanding User Journeys

narration.text: Beyond your application's internal code, its performance is often heavily influenced by external services it relies on. This is where the Dependencies blade in Application Insights becomes critical. It visualizes the performance and success rate of all calls your application makes to external services, such as databases, third-party APIs, or other Azure services. By analyzing dependency data, you can quickly pinpoint if a slowdown in your application is due to your own code or a sluggish downstream dependency. This is a common scenario and often overlooked. For example, if your database queries are consistently slow, the Dependencies blade will highlight this, guiding your optimization efforts. On the other hand, the Usage blade helps you understand how users interact with your application. It tracks user sessions, page views, and custom events, providing insights into user engagement, popular features, and navigation patterns. This data is invaluable for product managers and developers alike, helping to inform design decisions and identify areas where user experience can be improved. Together, these blades offer a comprehensive view of both your application's external interactions and its user-facing behavior.

keyIdea.title: Holistic Performance & User Insights
keyIdea.text: The Dependencies blade is crucial for identifying performance bottlenecks in external service calls, while the Usage blade helps understand user interactions and application adoption, providing a holistic view of application health and user experience.

narration.text: While Application Insights automatically collects a wealth of telemetry, there will often be specific business-level events or performance indicators that are unique to your application and not captured by default. This is where custom events and metrics become incredibly powerful. By using the Telemetry Client class in your application, you can explicitly log anything you need. For example, you can use Track Event to record when a user completes a specific action, like adding an item to a cart or completing a purchase, and attach custom properties like Order Id or Customer Tier. Similarly, Track Metric allows you to log numerical values, such as the total order amount or the duration of a specific internal process. You can also use Track Exception to log handled exceptions with additional context. It's important to call underscore telemetry Client. Flush open parenthesis close parenthesis in short-lived processes, like Azure Functions, to ensure telemetry is sent immediately before the process exits. This ability to customize telemetry allows you to gain deeper insights into user journeys, conversion funnels, and operational metrics that are directly relevant to your business logic, providing a truly tailored monitoring solution.

keyIdea.title: Tailored Business Telemetry
keyIdea.text: Custom events and metrics allow you to log specific business-level telemetry, providing deeper insights into user journeys, conversion funnels, and unique operational indicators beyond automatic collection.

content.html:
Module 6›Chapter 3›Custom Telemetry
Advanced Monitoring

Logging Custom Events and Metrics

Tailoring Telemetry for Business-Specific Insights

// Example: Logging a custom event and metric in .NET
using Microsoft.ApplicationInsights;
using Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.DataContracts;

public class OrderService
{
    private readonly TelemetryClient _telemetryClient;

    public OrderService(TelemetryClient telemetryClient)
    {
        _telemetryClient = telemetryClient;
    }

    public void ProcessOrder(string orderId, decimal amount)
    {
        // Log a custom event for order processing
        var eventTelemetry = new EventTelemetry("OrderProcessed");
        eventTelemetry.Properties["OrderId"] = orderId;
        eventTelemetry.Properties["CustomerTier"] = "Premium";
        _telemetryClient.TrackEvent(eventTelemetry);

        // Log a custom metric for order amount
        _telemetryClient.TrackMetric("OrderAmount", amount);

        // Simulate an exception
        if (amount > 1000)
        {
            throw new InvalidOperationException("Order amount exceeds limit.");
        }

        _telemetryClient.Flush(); // Ensure telemetry is sent immediately
    }
}
TrackEvent for Actions

Use TrackEvent to log specific user actions or business events, attaching custom properties for context.

TrackMetric for Values

Use TrackMetric to log numerical values, such as order amounts, processing times, or queue lengths.

TrackException for Handled Errors

Log handled exceptions with TrackException to capture errors that don't crash the application but are still important to monitor.

Key Takeaway

Custom telemetry allows you to extend Application Insights' capabilities, providing granular, business-specific insights that are crucial for understanding user behavior and operational efficiency.

screens.title: Querying Application Insights Data with KQL
screens.subtitle: Unlocking Deeper Insights with Log Analytics

narration.text: All the rich telemetry data collected by Application Insights isn't just displayed in pre-built charts and blades; it's also stored in a Log Analytics workspace. This integration is incredibly powerful because it means you can query your application's data using Kusto Query Language, or KQL. KQL is a powerful, read-only query language designed for big data analytics, and it allows you to perform complex queries, aggregations, and correlations across various data tables. Your Application Insights data is organized into specific tables like requests, dependencies, exceptions, traces, custom Events, and custom Metrics. This enables you to join application-level telemetry with infrastructure logs, providing a truly holistic view of your system. For instance, you could write a KQL query to find all requests that resulted in an exception and then correlate them with specific dependency calls that were slow. This capability is invaluable for advanced troubleshooting, identifying subtle patterns, and performing deep performance analysis that goes beyond what the standard portal views offer. Mastering KQL for Application Insights data unlocks a new level of diagnostic and optimization potential. Module 6›Chapter 3›Querying with KQL
Data Analysis

Querying Application Insights Data with KQL

Unlocking Deeper Insights with Log Analytics

Log Analytics Integration

Application Insights data is stored in a Log Analytics workspace, enabling powerful querying capabilities.

Kusto Query Language (KQL)

Use KQL to perform complex queries, aggregations, and correlations across your telemetry data.

Key Benefit

KQL allows you to correlate application-level telemetry with infrastructure logs, providing a truly holistic view of your system's health and performance.

// Example KQL Query
customEvents
| where name == "OrderProcessed"
| project TimeGenerated, name, customDimensions.OrderId, customMetrics.OrderValue
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Key Data Tables

Data is organized into tables like requests, dependencies, exceptions, traces, customEvents, and customMetrics.

Pro Tip

Start with simple queries and gradually add filters, aggregations, and joins to refine your analysis and uncover deeper insights.

Key Takeaway

KQL in Log Analytics is a powerful tool for advanced analysis of Application Insights data, enabling deep correlation and troubleshooting across your entire system.

narration.text: As we conclude this chapter, let's recap some of the essential concepts that form the foundation of Application Insights. First, remember that Application Performance Management, or APM, is about monitoring and managing the performance and availability of your software applications at a deep, code-level. Application Insights is Azure's robust solution for this. Second, the Application Insights SDK is the critical component you integrate directly into your application code. It's responsible for automatically collecting and sending all that valuable telemetry data to your Application Insights resource. Without the SDK, you wouldn't get those rich insights. Finally, the Instrumentation Key or Connection String acts as the unique identifier. It's the crucial link that connects your application's telemetry to its specific Application Insights resource in Azure, ensuring your data goes to the right place. Understanding these core ideas is fundamental to effectively leveraging Application Insights for your monitoring needs.

keyIdea.title: Foundational APM Principles
keyIdea.text: Mastering these foundational concepts—APM, the Application Insights SDK, and the Instrumentation Key—is crucial for effectively leveraging Application Insights to monitor and optimize your applications.

content.html:
Module 6›Chapter 3›Key Concepts

Essential Application Insights Concepts

Core Ideas for APM Success

Application Performance Management (APM)

Tools and practices for monitoring and managing the performance and availability of software applications.

Application Insights SDK

Libraries integrated into application code to automatically collect and send telemetry data to Application Insights.

Instrumentation Key/Connection String

A unique identifier that links your application's telemetry to a specific Application Insights resource.

Summary Takeaway

Application Insights provides comprehensive APM through its SDK, which uses an Instrumentation Key to send rich telemetry data for deep application monitoring and diagnostics.

narration.text: Let's reinforce the key features that make Application Insights an indispensable tool for developers. The Live Metrics Stream offers a real-time, minute-by-minute view of your application's performance and health. This is incredibly useful for immediate operational awareness, especially during deployments. Next, Transaction Search is a powerful diagnostic feature that allows you to search for individual telemetry items and view the complete end-to-end transaction flow. This capability is invaluable for debugging specific user issues or understanding complex interactions across multiple services. Finally, Custom Events and Metrics represent the extensibility of Application Insights. These are user-defined telemetry points that you log from your application code to track specific business logic or performance indicators. This allows you to gather insights that are unique to your application's domain, going beyond the automatically collected data. Together, these features provide unparalleled visibility and control over your application's operational health and user experience.

keyIdea.title: Powerful Diagnostic Capabilities
keyIdea.text: Application Insights provides powerful features like Live Metrics, Transaction Search, and Custom Events/Metrics to give you unparalleled visibility into your application's health and user behavior.

Summary Takeaway

Application Insights offers a suite of powerful features, from real-time monitoring with Live Metrics to detailed transaction tracing and custom telemetry, providing comprehensive diagnostic capabilities for any application.
